summary.headline: AAVAS Q2FY27: AUM up 16.1% YoY to ₹248.0 bn, H1 disbursements ₹35.1 bn (+30% YoY), cost-to-income down to 42.9%.
summary.overview: Management reported H1FY27 net profit up 16.4% YoY to ₹3.5 bn, with NII up 17% YoY and cost-to-income improving 195 bps YoY to 42.9%. Asset quality improved YoY, with 1+ DPD at 3.81% and Net Stage 3 at 0.70%. Management said AUM is on track to cross ₹250 bn in October 2026, and reiterated a 5%+ spread commitment despite a 25 bps repo hike earlier in October, with cost of borrowing expected to rise. The call was heavily focused on RO productivity, spread defence, LAP/HL mix shift, and insurance fee dependence.

segments.name: Home loans (HL) vs non-HL
segments.commentary: Target steady-state AUM mix is 65:35 HL to non-HL. Top-up loans to existing customers (about 5% of disbursements) are tagged as LAP, and booking above 60% construction stage is classed as LAP, which lifted LAP to about 21% of H1 disbursements versus about 14% of AUM.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME disbursement growth slowed to about 18% YoY in Q2 from about 32% previously. Management said this reflects risk and pricing discipline, not caution.

segments.name: Insurance fee income
segments.commentary: Insurance income is about 4% of PBT. Management aims to close about 50% of the regulatory revenue gap from 1 April 2027 by raising attachment rates.

guidance_outlook: Crossing ₹250 bn AUM in October 2026, with a long-term ambition of ₹500 bn AUM.
Management guided to AUM growth of 16-17% for FY27, and to disbursement growth of 20%+.
Spreads to stay above 5% on placements and at book level, even after the 25 bps repo hike, with cost of borrowing expected to rise and NIM and spreads expected to improve over coming quarters.
Productivity target of about 1.5 files per RO per month by end-FY27, scaling to 2 files; cost-to-income to fall below 40% medium term; opex-to-assets to fall below 3% (currently 3.33% in H1FY27).
Credit cost guidance within 25 bps; H1FY27 credit cost was 24 bps. Repayment rate expected at about 17%.
Medium-term volume growth build-up: about 20%+ CAGR, of which about 8% from branches, 10% from productivity and 5-7% from ATS.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 443 across 15 states at end-Q2; further branch expansion planned, with focus on faster branch breakeven.
Long-term incentive plan rolled out mid-Q2; ESOP running for about 200 employees.
Headcount down about 150; management said this reflects repurposing and right-sizing, not job cuts.
demand_pricing: RO productivity: 1.1 files/month in Q1FY27, 1.2 in Q2FY27, 1.3 in September 2026. Revenue per RO up 29% in H1.
Home loan incremental yields have moved up about 8-10 bps; management said home loans are highly competitive.
PLR unchanged after the 25 bps repo hike; ALCO reviews PLR monthly.
Management said larger HFCs target a different ATS segment, so it sees no direct competitive pressure.
Borrowing mix: about 30% linked to repo; ₹16.79 bn raised in Q2FY27 at 7.66%.
Liquidity: ₹19.6 bn cash and un-availed CC limits, plus ₹3 bn documented un-availed sanctions.

qa_highlights.question: How has mortgage performance been in past weak monsoon or drought periods, and how does this affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mortgages have stayed resilient, lead indicators are improving month on month, and agri-income exposure is very limited. Exposure to Marathwada districts such as Latur is minimal.

qa_highlights.question: Will spreads be defended and will the 5% spread hold as repo-linked borrowings reprice in Q3 without a PLR hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated spreads above 5%, said incremental spreads are almost the same as the book spread today, and said PLR will be raised if ALCO sees the need.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to ₹500 bn AUM, and what drives growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management broke the volume growth build-up into about 8% from branches, 10% from productivity and 5-7% from ATS, consistent with about 20%+ volume CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the increase in LAP share, and what is the target HL/NHL mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-ups to existing customers are booked as LAP, and construction-stage clarification moved bookings above 60% completion into LAP. Steady-state AUM target is 65:35 HL to NHL.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the MSME disbursement growth slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter of matching placements to risk and pricing, and that a quarterly change in mix should not be over-read.

qa_highlights.question: What is the insurance-fee risk from upcoming regulation, and how far can opex fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to recover about 50% of the expected regulatory loss by raising attachment rates, and to move cost-to-income below 40% in the medium term. Insurance is about 4% of PBT.

risks_watch: Cost of borrowing rising after the 25 bps repo hike, with about 30% of borrowings repo-linked; the spread defence depends on pricing pass-through and no PLR change so far.
Regulatory change to insurance distribution from 1 April 2027 could reduce fee income; management is targeting roughly half the expected loss to be recovered.
Productivity at 1.3 files per RO per month still short of the 1.5 target; scaling to 2 files depends on top-of-funnel growth.
Monsoon deficits in some states, with Maharashtra at about 19% of exposure; management says impact is minimal, but this needs monitoring.
Slower MSME disbursement growth (about 18% vs 32% earlier) and the HL/LAP reclassification could affect yield mix.
Headcount reduction of about 150 and a revamped incentive structure could affect frontline attrition.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, liabilities and spreads, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the spread outlook and PLR, repeatedly stressing the 5% floor. Management was more evasive on specific numbers such as the Q2 MSME slowdown and the reasons for the LAP share increase.
key_quotes: Following the 25-bps repo rate increase announced by the RBI earlier this month, we expect our cost of borrowing to increase.
I do not see Aavas having any hiccups on asset quality at all.
We are not cutting down on people.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 443 branches across 15 states at end-Q2 with further expansion planned but no count given; productivity target of 1.5 files/RO/month by end-FY27 relies on existing network rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guided AUM growth 16-17% and disbursement growth 20%+ for FY27; H1 disbursements ₹35.1 bn were up 30% YoY, and AUM is on track to cross ₹250 bn in October 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; no utilisation figure is given for a lending business.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated existing guidance (AUM 16-17%, disbursements 20%+, spreads above 5%) without raising it, and H1 AUM growth of 16.1% sits within the guided range.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost of borrowing is expected to rise after the 25 bps repo hike with ~30% of borrowings repo-linked, and the 5% spread floor depends on pass-through with no PLR change yet; insurance regulation from 1 April 2027 could cut fee income (insurance ~4% of PBT).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed; LAP/HL mix shift is a reclassification, not a launch.

rows.label: PLR revision to defend spreads
rows.why: Management said PLR will be raised if ALCO sees the need, with PLR unchanged after the 25 bps repo hike and reviewed monthly; repo-linked borrowings are about 30% of the total.

rows.label: Insurance distribution regulation from 1 April 2027
rows.why: Management expects a regulatory revenue loss on insurance fees (about 4% of PBT) and targets recovering about 50% via higher attachment rates.

rows.label: Opex-to-assets below 3% medium term
rows.why: Opex-to-assets is 3.33% in H1FY27 and cost-to-income fell to 42.9%; the target of below 40% depends on RO productivity rising from 1.3 toward 1.5 files per month.
